To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PGE2 inhibits interleukin 1 production in human T lymphocytes by inhibiting the phosphorylation of pp21 and 23 cytosolic proteins.

PGE2 inhibits interleukin 1 and 2 production by human T cells, and that this inhibition is mediated by cAMP-dependent protein kinases, which in turn inhibit the phosphorylation of cytosolic proteins pp21 and pp 23.

prostaglandin-E2 (PGE) inhibits the activation of T lymphocytes by inhibiting the phosphorylation of pp21 and 23, and that PGE does this by inhibiting the cAMP-dependent kinase, which is involved in the phosphorylation of the two proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular events occurring after the triggering of the CD3-T cell receptor complex by anti-CD2 and anti-CD3 mAbs.
the study of the mechanisms of the inhibitory effect of PGE2 on T cell activation.
the biochemical events involved in the regulation of interleukin-2 (IL-2) synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PGE2 inhibits the phosphorylation of cytosolic proteins by inhibiting the activity of the cAMP dependent protein kinase and that the inhibition of the phosphorylation by the cAMP dependent kinase is an essential step in T lymphocyte activation, leading to the production of interleukin-2.

PGE2, by activating cAMP-dependent protein kinases and inhibiting Ca2+/phospholipid-dependent protein kinases, inhibits T cell proliferation by decreasing the expression of interleukin 1 receptor, interleukin 4 receptor, and interleukin-2 receptor, by decreasing interleukin-1 and interleukin production, and by inhibiting the expression of the interleukin-3 gene.
the cAMP-dependent kinase is a major regulator of T lymphocyte function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cAMP-dependent protein kinases are involved in T cell activation and that they are involved in the regulation of interleukin-2 synthesis.

the modulation of T lymphocyte function is a consequence of the differential regulation of the protein phosphorylation of two specific cytosolic proteins by cAMP-dependent and Ca2+/phospholipid-dependent protein kinases, which are activated by PGE2 and anti-CD3 mAb, respectively.
the phosphorylation of cytosolic proteins is essential to T cell activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a new class of proteins that are involved in T cell activation.
the modulation of pp21 phosphorylation is a key event for the regulation of T cell activation and interleukin-2 production.
there are a lot of different ways in which the immune system is regulated, and that it's not a simple on/off switch.
